onsiteWorkflow: Before the visit, ask Clinton Library staff whether the 2013-0185-M OA/ID folders can be pre-pulled, whether any folders are fully or partly withdrawn, and whether there are daily pull or scanning limits.
Use the first pull for European Affairs policy-core folders before speechwriting or broad crisis folders.
For every folder opened, photograph or transcribe the folder title, OA/ID number, collection path, withdrawal sheets, and first/last page before extracting document images.
Promote only document-level items into the public corpus after recording actual date, sender/recipient or meeting participants, page span, markings, release status, and source-note path.
Use Executive Secretary trip books and PC/DC files to settle chronology, then use Speechwriting files as public-text controls rather than as the main documentary base.
Keep a same-day decision log: include candidate, context only, duplicate/source-control, or no action.
questionsForArchivist: Can these OA/ID folders be requested in advance from release 2013-0185-M?
Are any of the listed folders available as digital surrogates or already-scanned researcher copies?
What are current pull limits, reproduction limits, and citation preferences for Clinton Presidential Records, NSC folder-title files?
Do folder titles map directly to box requests, or should the researcher request by office/staff segment plus OA/ID number?
Are withdrawal sheets available at the folder level and should they be cited separately when a document is partially withheld?
